artist.mediums: Kerala mural painting (acrylic on canvas), watercolour, coloured pencil
artist.about:
Mahi (Maheshwaran) is a self-taught painter of Kerala murals, the temple-wall art of Kerala: gods and goddesses drawn in bold outline, filled with ochre, red, green and blue, and framed with rich ornament and lotus borders.

He began in Sydney in 2016 with a large Rasa Leela, Krishna dancing among the gopis, which travelled with him between Sydney and India for six years before he redrew and finished it in 2022. During the lockdown years he worked through a numbered series of paintings, learning the style's fine-line Rekhikam shading as he went, and decided to stay with traditional colours, traditional methods and free-hand drawing.

His work ranges from Krishna, Radha, Ganesha, Shiva and Shankaranarayana to Saraswati and Hanuman, mostly in acrylic on canvas, with some watercolour and coloured-pencil pieces.
artist.training: Self-taught; learnt the traditional techniques, such as Rekhikam fine-line shading, through practice and online lessons
artist.experience: Painting Kerala murals since 2016, in Sydney, India and California. Large works include the Rasa Leela (2016 to 2022) and The Butter Thieves.

works.title: Rasa Leela
works.description: Artist's note: every painting has its own destiny. I started this one in Sydney on 18 February 2016, and thought it was 80% done. It travelled with me to India and back, and waited at my parents' house for years. When I picked it up again I had grown as a painter, so I redrew the whole painting and finished it on 15 November 2022: born in Sydney, it finally reached its home.

works.title: Shankaranarayana
works.medium: Kerala mural painting, acrylic on canvas
works.description: Artist's note: painting no. 4. With new-found confidence, it was time to go fully traditional. I added something of my own to the reference painting, some ornaments and the tree behind, and from here on decided to stick to traditional colours and methods, and only free-hand drawing.

works.title: Ganesha II
works.description: Artist's note: I drew this baby Ganesha to give to someone, but predictably fell in love with him and decided to keep him. The story doesn't end there…

works.title: Little Ganesha
works.medium: Kerala mural painting, acrylic on canvas
works.description: Artist's note: I don't want to give you away to anyone, my child. Be with me forever. This little one took 10 hours to complete. Painted in Macquarie Fields, Sydney.

works.title: Ganesha (watercolour)
works.medium: Kerala mural style, watercolour and ink on paper
works.description: Artist's note: I drew the earlier little Ganesha for my neighbour's mother, who was leaving for India, but loved him too much to part with him, so I quickly painted another Ganesha. This is that one.

works.title: Ganesha on the Lotus Throne
works.description: Artist's note: a Ganesha painting for my sister, one of my quickest works. Painted in Los Gatos, California.

works.title: Radha Madhavam
works.description: Artist's note: I'm reluctant to part with my paintings except with people who are close to me and appreciate the effort that goes into each piece. This was the first time I made a painting specifically for someone: for our friends' new house in Sydney.

works.title: Vishnu on Adisesha
works.description: Artist's note: my first mural after almost a year and a half. Though it is a copy of a Mattancherry Palace mural, I drew the sketch by the traditional “Thalapramanam” proportion rule, Dasathalam (ten parts). I shortened the left thigh, then found the garland and ornaments made it look stunted, so I had to erase and correct it. Rules are not made for fun; lesson learnt.

works.title: Woman with a Basket of Lotuses
works.description: Artist's note: a quick one to practise Kerala murals, picking up the brushes after six months. Painted in Macquarie Fields, Sydney.

works.title: Tulips and Calla Lilies
works.description: Artist's note: my quickest acrylic painting, done just to use up the last canvas in a pack of three. Painted in Los Gatos, California.

works.title: Ardhanari with Ganesha and Murugan
works.description: Artist's note: painting no. 7. I wanted to break away from “photocopying” but lacked the confidence to go big, so I started on a modest A3 canvas, taking reference from a favourite sketch by the legendary Bapu Ramana. I'll draw this on a bigger canvas with more detail in future.

works.title: Shiva and Parvati Dancing
works.description: Artist's note: painting no. 8, my first ever original composition, on leftover canvas cloth slightly longer than A3. I tried to create “dancing vibes”. Every painting coincided with some event: this one was finished the day Sydney's lockdown eased after 136 days.
